report.summary: Comparing the two complete months available, August and September 2026, net sales fell by 8500 cents. Gross sales rose, but the increase in refunds more than offset that growth; the records do not establish why refunds increased.

findings.statement: Overall net sales moved from 191500 cents in August to 183000 cents in September, a decline of 8500 cents.
Gross sales increased by 10000 cents, while refunds increased by 18500 cents, accounting for the net decline.

The small segment's refunds grew from 2500 cents to 16000 cents, and its net sales fell from 56500 cents to 49000 cents. The large segment's net sales fell from 135000 cents to 134000 cents; segment totals reconcile to overall totals.
The records do not say why customers requested refunds, so the underlying cause of the increase cannot be determined.

assumptions: Chose the two complete months in the data, August 1–September 1 and September 1–October 1, 2026, rather than partial October; dates are UTC, with the start included and end excluded.
Amounts are integer USD cents. Gross sales use order dates; refunds use refund dates; net sales equal gross minus refunds.
Refunds are attributed to the segment of the customer on the original order. August and September segment figures reconcile to independently calculated overall totals.
open_questions: What reasons were recorded for the September refunds, if available in another system?
Were any particular products or operational issues associated with the refunded orders?

queries.purpose: Identify available dates and monthly gross sales and refunds to select comparison periods.
queries.sql: WITH order_months AS (SELECT substr(order_date,1,7) AS month, SUM(amount_cents) AS gross FROM orders GROUP BY 1), refund_months AS (SELECT substr(refund_date,1,7) AS month, SUM(amount_cents) AS refunds FROM refunds GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(o.month,r.month) AS month, COALESCE(o.gross,0) AS gross, COALESCE(r.refunds,0) AS refunds, COALESCE(o.gross,0)-COALESCE(r.refunds,0) AS net FROM order_months o FULL OUTER JOIN refund_months r ON o.month=r.month ORDER BY month

queries.purpose: Compare August and September sales and refunds by customer segment, alongside reconciled overall totals.
queries.sql: WITH periods AS (SELECT '2026-08-01' AS start_date,'2026-09-01' AS end_date UNION ALL SELECT '2026-09-01','2026-10-01'), segments AS (SELECT segment FROM customers UNION ALL SELECT NULL), order_totals AS (SELECT p.start_date,c.segment,SUM(o.amount_cents) AS gross FROM periods p JOIN orders o ON o.order_date>=p.start_date AND o.order_date<p.end_date JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id GROUP BY p.start_date,c.segment), refund_totals AS (SELECT p.start_date,c.segment,SUM(r.amount_cents) AS refunds FROM periods p JOIN refunds r ON r.refund_date>=p.start_date AND r.refund_date<p.end_date JOIN orders o ON r.order_id=o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id GROUP BY p.start_date,c.segment), combined AS (SELECT p.start_date,p.end_date,s.segment,COALESCE(ot.gross,0) AS gross,COALESCE(rt.refunds,0) AS refunds FROM periods p CROSS JOIN segments s LEFT JOIN order_totals ot ON ot.start_date=p.start_date AND ot.segment=s.segment LEFT JOIN refund_totals rt ON rt.start_date=p.start_date AND rt.segment=s.segment), output AS (SELECT start_date,end_date,segment,gross,refunds,gross-refunds AS net FROM combined WHERE segment IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT start_date,end_date,NULL,SUM(gross),SUM(refunds),SUM(gross-refunds) FROM combined WHERE segment IS NOT NULL GROUP BY start_date,end_date) SELECT * FROM output ORDER BY start_date,segment IS NOT NULL,segment

queries.purpose: Correct segment breakdown and verify segment sums against independently calculated monthly overall totals.
queries.sql: WITH periods AS (SELECT '2026-08-01' AS start_date,'2026-09-01' AS end_date UNION ALL SELECT '2026-09-01','2026-10-01'), order_totals AS (SELECT p.start_date,c.segment,SUM(o.amount_cents) AS gross FROM periods p JOIN orders o ON o.order_date>=p.start_date AND o.order_date<p.end_date JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id GROUP BY p.start_date,c.segment), refund_totals AS (SELECT p.start_date,c.segment,SUM(r.amount_cents) AS refunds FROM periods p JOIN refunds r ON r.refund_date>=p.start_date AND r.refund_date<p.end_date JOIN orders o ON o.order_id=r.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id GROUP BY p.start_date,c.segment), segments AS (SELECT segment FROM customers GROUP BY segment), segment_data AS (SELECT p.start_date,p.end_date,s.segment,COALESCE(ot.gross,0) AS gross,COALESCE(rt.refunds,0) AS refunds FROM periods p CROSS JOIN segments s LEFT JOIN order_totals ot ON ot.start_date=p.start_date AND ot.segment=s.segment LEFT JOIN refund_totals rt ON rt.start_date=p.start_date AND rt.segment=s.segment), independent AS (SELECT p.start_date,COALESCE((SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM orders WHERE order_date>=p.start_date AND order_date<p.end_date),0) AS gross,COALESCE((SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM refunds WHERE refund_date>=p.start_date AND refund_date<p.end_date),0) AS refunds FROM periods p) SELECT d.start_date,d.end_date,d.segment,d.gross,d.refunds,d.gross-d.refunds AS net,i.gross-SUM(d.gross) OVER (PARTITION BY d.start_date) AS gross_reconciliation_difference,i.refunds-SUM(d.refunds) OVER (PARTITION BY d.start_date) AS refunds_reconciliation_difference FROM segment_data d JOIN independent i ON i.start_date=d.start_date UNION ALL SELECT d.start_date,d.end_date,NULL,SUM(d.gross),SUM(d.refunds),SUM(d.gross)-SUM(d.refunds),i.gross-SUM(d.gross),i.refunds-SUM(d.refunds) FROM segment_data d JOIN independent i ON i.start_date=d.start_date GROUP BY d.start_date,d.end_date,i.gross,i.refunds ORDER BY start_date,segment IS NOT NULL,segment

messages.content:
You investigate questions about a fictional company's sales with read-only SQL over a small SQLite database.

## How to work

1. Call `run_sql` for a first look. Compute every figure in SQL, not in your head.
2. Read the result, then choose at least one follow-up query based on it, for example separating gross sales from refunds or comparing customer segments.
3. You have at most 6 query attempts, and errors count. Two to four queries are usually enough.
4. Call `submit_report` once the results answer the question.

## Metric rules in SQL

- Apply the business rules below even where they differ from the usual meaning of a metric name.
- Use half-open periods: `order_date >= '2026-08-01' AND order_date < '2026-09-01'`. Filter refunds by `refund_date`, never by the date of their order.
- Aggregate orders and refunds in separate subqueries, then combine them. Joining refund rows to orders repeats order amounts.
- Join only on keys: `refunds.order_id = orders.order_id` and `orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id`. A refund's segment is the segment of the customer on its original order.
- Keep each query to one breakdown, and give CTEs names that differ from the table names.
- Before you report a breakdown, check that its parts add up to the overall totals. If they do not, fix the query.

## Report

- Every figure in `metrics` must appear exactly as a cell in the result of the query it cites, for example `q2`. Query any total or segment figure you need.
- Attach every amount you mention to a finding's `metrics`. A change between periods is the one exception: attach the figure for each period and write only the difference in the text.
- In text, write money only as an integer followed by "cents", for example "183000 cents". Do not use "$" or dollars; the application formats money.
- `observed`: shown directly by a query result. `inferred`: a conclusion drawn from observed figures. `unknown`: something the data cannot establish. Refund rows record amounts and dates, not why customers asked for refunds, so do not guess causes.
- State the periods, units and any other assumption. If the question does not name periods, choose them from the data and say so.

# Business data investigation: exercise rules

These fictional rules are the source of truth for this assignment. No industry research is required.

1. Use customers, orders, and refunds. IDs link refunds to orders and orders to customers; one order can have multiple refunds.
2. Gross sales for a period sum orders by order_date. Refunds for that period sum refunds by refund_date. Net sales equal gross sales minus refunds. Use UTC dates and half-open periods: start included, end excluded.
3. Use integer USD cents. Group order and refund totals separately before combining them; joining raw refund rows to orders can repeat order amounts.
4. Assign refunds to the segment of the customer on the original order. The records show amounts and dates, not why a customer requested a refund.

## Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE customers (customer_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, segment TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (order_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(customer_id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(amount_cents >= 0));
CREATE TABLE refunds (refund_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(order_id), refund_date TEXT NOT NULL, amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(amount_cents >= 0));
```

start_date,'2026-09-01' AS end_date UNION ALL SELECT '2026-09-01','2026-10-01'), order_totals AS (SELECT p.start_date,c.segment,SUM(o.amount_cents) AS gross FROM periods p JOIN orders o ON o.order_date>=p.start_date AND o.order_date<p.end_date JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id GROUP BY p.start_date,c.segment), refund_totals AS (SELECT p.start_date,c.segment,SUM(r.amount_cents) AS refunds FROM periods p JOIN refunds r ON r.refund_date>=p.start_date AND r.refund_date<p.end_date JOIN orders o ON o.order_id=r.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id GROUP BY p.start_date,c.segment), segments AS (SELECT segment FROM customers GROUP BY segment), segment_data AS (SELECT p.start_date,p.end_date,s.segment,COALESCE(ot.gross,0) AS gross,COALESCE(rt.refunds,0) AS refunds FROM periods p CROSS JOIN segments s LEFT JOIN order_totals ot ON ot.start_date=p.start_date AND ot.segment=s.segment LEFT JOIN refund_totals rt ON rt.start_date=p.start_date AND rt.segment=s.segment), independent AS (SELECT p.start_date,COALESCE((SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM orders WHERE order_date>=p.start_date AND order_date<p.end_date),0) AS gross,COALESCE((SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM refunds WHERE refund_date>=p.start_date AND refund_date<p.end_date),0) AS refunds FROM periods p), output AS (SELECT d.start_date,d.end_date,d.segment,d.gross,d.refunds,d.gross-d.refunds AS net,i.gross-SUM(d.gross) OVER (PARTITION BY d.start_date) AS gross_check,i.refunds-SUM(d.refunds) OVER (PARTITION BY d.start_date) AS refunds_check FROM segment_data d JOIN independent i ON i.start_date=d.start_date UNION ALL SELECT d.start_date,d.end_date,NULL,SUM(d.gross),SUM(d.refunds),SUM(d.gross)-SUM(d.refunds),i.gross-SUM(d.gross),i.refunds-SUM(d.refunds) FROM segment_data d JOIN independent i ON i.start_date=d.start_date GROUP BY d.start_date,d.end_date,i.gross,i.refunds) SELECT * FROM output ORDER BY start_date,segment IS NOT NULL,segment"}
